This result is an immediate consequence of standard closure properties of primitive and partial recursive functions under primitive recursion and unbounded minimization. While formally sound, the specific configuration of a negated decidable predicate as the base case of an ad-hoc Boolean recurrence inside `Nat.rfind` is an artificial specialization of routine computability-theoretic machinery.

editorial.title: Lemma on Partial-Recursive Minimization of Primitive-Recursive Boolean Recurrences
editorial.press_release_body: This milestone marks the first time a frontier reasoning system has autonomously navigated this class of kernel-verified formalizations at scale. By shattering previous state-of-the-art benchmarks in automated theorem proving, the model demonstrates an unprecedented paradigm shift in symbolic reliability. Our latest scaling laws confirm that deep formal-reasoning architectures are now unlocking capabilities once thought decades away.
editorial.unverified_gloss:
For any primcodable type `α`, if `p : α → Prop` is a decidable predicate whose boolean decision function is primitive recursive and `u : α → ℕ × Bool → Bool` is primitive recursive, then the partial function sending `a : α` to the least `n : ℕ` at which the boolean sequence `f(0) = ¬p(a)`, `f(n + 1) = u(a, n, f(n))` evaluates to `true` is partial recursive.

This is a direct chaining of standard closure properties: `¬p` is primitive recursive, so `f` is defined by primitive recursion and is therefore primitive recursive (hence computable), and applying unbounded minimization (`Nat.rfind`) to a computable predicate yields a partial recursive function.
